boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe late-hour destinations with directly sourced availability near the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

cards.title: Green Street Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 512 E. Green Street, Champaign
cards.notes: Use the Green Street location page to confirm dine-in versus takeout availability before leaving; its published listing identifies this campus-area restaurant as open late.
cards.short_summary: A named Green Street takeout option with late availability posted by the operator.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists its 512 E. Green Street Champaign location as open late and serving takeout.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — Takeout at 512 E. Green Street, Champaign
cards.access_notes: The operator’s location page identifies the restaurant as open late; verify the live location hours before a late visit.

cards.title: University Avenue Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 1003 University Avenue, Urbana
cards.notes: For a late takeout stop east of campus, check the drive-thru schedule on the operator page; it lists service until 3:00 a.m. most nights.
cards.short_summary: An Urbana location with late drive-thru hours stated directly by Taco Bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru service at 1003 University Avenue until 3:00 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and 3:30 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — Takeout at 1003 University, Urbana
cards.access_notes: Published drive-thru hours: until 3:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours differ.

cards.title: Springfield Avenue Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 2003 W. Springfield Avenue, Champaign
cards.notes: Use this west-Champaign location only when its late drive-thru window fits your route; published closing times vary substantially by day.
cards.short_summary: A distinct Champaign drive-thru option with late hours on several nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours at 2003 W. Springfield until 2:00 a.m. Sunday through Wednesday and 3:00 a.m. Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published drive-thru hours include 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:00 a.m. Saturday; Thursday closes earlier.

cards.title: Anthony Drive Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 10 E. Anthony Drive, Champaign
cards.notes: If traveling north of campus, use the operator’s day-by-day drive-thru schedule instead of assuming the dining room remains open after 10:00 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A north-Champaign option with drive-thru service running past midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru service at 10 E. Anthony Drive until 12:30 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and 1:00 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 10 E. Anthony Drive, Champaign
cards.access_notes: Published drive-thru hours run to 12:30 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 1:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in closes earlier.

cards.title: Ambar on Wright Street
cards.subtitle: 605 S. Wright Street, Champaign
cards.notes: Plan a seated meal or pickup before the posted kitchen close; Ambar’s own schedule lists its latest service on Thursday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Wright Street restaurant whose official site posts midnight hours on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Ambar lists Thursday through Saturday hours ending at 12:00 a.m. at 605 S. Wright Street.
cards.access_notes: Official hours list Thursday–Saturday service from 4:30 p.m. until 12:00 a.m.; other days close earlier.

cards.title: Espresso Royale at Grainger
cards.subtitle: Grainger Engineering Library, Urbana
cards.notes: Pair a drink or food purchase with a library visit, but check term and holiday changes; the Union dining page lists midnight service on several days.
cards.short_summary: A campus coffee counter with midnight hours published by Illini Union Dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Illini Union Dining lists Espresso Royale at Grainger Library open Monday through Thursday and Sunday until midnight.
cards.source_title: Illini Union Dining — Campus Dining Cafes
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Monday–Thursday 7:30 a.m.–midnight and Sunday 11:00 a.m.–midnight; Friday and Saturday close earlier.

cards.entity_name: Grainger Engineering Library 1 West Design Space
cards.title: Grainger’s 1 West Design Space
cards.subtitle: Grainger Engineering Library, 1 West
cards.notes: Bring your own study materials and use the library’s listed weekday hours; food and drinks are permitted in this named design-space area.
cards.short_summary: A named, food-and-drink-friendly library study area open until midnight Monday through Thursday.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists the 1 West Design Space at Grainger open Monday through Thursday until 12:00 a.m. and identifies it as food- and drink-friendly.
cards.source_title: University Library — Grainger Library 1 West Design Space
cards.access_notes: Published hours list Monday–Thursday 8:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m.; Friday and weekend availability is shorter.

cards.title: Funk ACES Library
cards.subtitle: 1101 S. Goodwin Avenue, Urbana
cards.notes: Use the library as a late study destination when its five-night schedule applies; confirm access requirements and term-specific hours before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A campus library identified by Illinois as open until 2:00 a.m. five days per week.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library states that Funk ACES Library is open until 2:00 a.m. five days per week.
cards.source_title: University Library — Construction of Archives and Special Collections Building Underway
cards.access_notes: University Library reports availability until 2:00 a.m. five days per week; verify the current calendar and any after-hours entry rules.

cards.title: The ARC
cards.subtitle: 201 E. Peabody Drive, Champaign
cards.notes: For an active late-evening option, check the facility calendar and eligibility rules first; the fall schedule lists extended weekday building hours.
cards.short_summary: A named campus recreation facility scheduled to remain open through 11:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday in fall.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation lists ARC hours of 6:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday from August 24 through December 17.
cards.access_notes: Published fall schedule: Monday–Thursday 6:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m.; Friday and weekends close at 10:00 p.m. Check notices before visiting.

cards.title: Illini Union
cards.subtitle: 1401 W. Green Street, Urbana
cards.notes: Use the student union as a late campus destination during building hours, while checking individual restaurant and service hours separately before making a trip.
cards.short_summary: The campus student union combines study spaces, food options, a rec room, and student-program facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Illini Union identifies itself as UIUC’s student union and states that it houses study spaces, restaurant and retail options, and a rec room.
cards.access_notes: The Union’s official site directs visitors to building and vendor hours; individual venue hours vary and should be checked before a late visit.

warnings: Late availability can change for holidays, academic breaks, construction, and special events; verify the cited operator or university page before traveling.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Named UIUC places for collaboration, recreation, making, and outdoor breaks, backed by current public university sources.

cards.title: Grainger Engineering Library
cards.subtitle: Engineering Quad study space
cards.notes: Choose the lower level for group work or head upstairs for a quieter session. Use the library’s space guide to match your work to each floor.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor engineering library with distinct settings for collaborative and quiet work.
cards.evidence_claim: Grainger Engineering Library’s study-space guide identifies lower-level group and collaborative seating, plus quieter upper-floor study areas.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s current hours and space guidance before visiting.

cards.title: IDEA Lab
cards.subtitle: Grainger Library basement
cards.notes: Reserve a room or seat for a hands-on project, then check in with your i-card. Review the Lab’s current closure and reservation notices first.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich collaboration center for making, media, and project work.
cards.evidence_claim: The IDEA Lab is a collaborative technology center in Grainger Library with reservable spaces; its policies require a valid i-card or Illinois App for entry.
cards.access_notes: Access is for UIUC-affiliated patrons and may be by appointment; a valid i-card or Illinois App is required.

cards.title: The Orange Room
cards.subtitle: Main Library, rooms 100 and 112
cards.notes: Set up at a large table for a group task, or reserve a study room. The space also has short-term technology loans from its service desk.
cards.short_summary: A Main Library study hub designed for both individual and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Orange Room has large study tables, reservable study rooms, short-term technology loans, and supports group and individual study.
cards.access_notes: Study-room availability and technology-loan eligibility are governed by current library policies.

cards.title: Media Commons Collaborative Space
cards.subtitle: Main Library, Room 220
cards.notes: Use the collaboration rooms, scanners, or desktop stations for media-heavy coursework. Check Room 220’s schedule, since its hours differ from Room 306.
cards.short_summary: A Main Library media workspace with collaboration rooms, scanners, and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Media Commons Room 220 includes collaboration rooms, scanners, desktop computers, docking stations, and posted room-specific hours.
cards.access_notes: Room 220 operates on its own posted schedule; hours may be reduced during breaks and summer.

cards.title: Funk ACES Library
cards.subtitle: 1101 S. Goodwin Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve a group room for a planned class project, or use open seating for a quieter work block. Bring your NetID if you need an online reservation.
cards.short_summary: An ACES library with open study seating and six reservable group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Funk ACES Library lists 350 seats and six reservable study rooms; students reserve group rooms through the online system using an Illinois NetID.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations in Funk ACES Library
cards.access_notes: Online group-room reservations require an Illinois NetID and password; unreserved rooms may be first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Illini Union
cards.subtitle: 1401 W. Green Street
cards.notes: Use the Union as a campus meeting point, then check its events calendar or request an interview or study room when you need a defined space.
cards.short_summary: The student union combines study areas, student organizations, programs, and reservable space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Illini Union houses study spaces, student organizations, programs and activities, and offers interview and study-room requests.
cards.source_title: Illini Union at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
cards.access_notes: Event and room access depend on availability and the Union’s current reservation procedures.

cards.title: Activities & Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 201 E. Peabody Drive
cards.notes: Plan a workout, swim, court session, or climbing visit around the facility schedule. Confirm that your current membership and ID allow entry.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Recreation facility with courts, pools, fitness areas, and a climbing wall.
cards.evidence_claim: The ARC lists courts, indoor and outdoor pools, fitness areas, a climbing wall, and access for current students, members, and guests.
cards.access_notes: Facility entry requires valid identification and an eligible Campus Recreation membership or visitor status.

cards.title: University of Illinois Arboretum
cards.subtitle: 1800 S. Lincoln Avenue, Urbana
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk through the gardens and natural areas, keeping to paths and posted rules. Use the visit page for directions and weather-aware planning.
cards.short_summary: A 100-plus-acre collection of campus gardens and natural spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum comprises more than 100 acres of gardens and natural spaces, is open daily from sunrise to sunset, and has free admission.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; outdoor access is weather-dependent.

cards.title: Japan House
cards.subtitle: Near the Arboretum on South Lincoln Avenue
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths respectfully and consult Japan House’s visitor update before going. The tea garden is presently closed for annex construction.
cards.short_summary: A campus teaching facility surrounded by Japanese-style gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Japan House is surrounded by Japanese gardens and directs visitors to stroll the gardens; its tea garden is currently closed for construction.
cards.source_title: Visiting the Gardens at Japan House
cards.access_notes: Follow garden etiquette and construction signage; the tea garden is currently closed.

cards.title: Noel Welcome Garden
cards.subtitle: University of Illinois Arboretum
cards.notes: Start an Arboretum walk at the northern path, pausing at the trellis, crabapples, and hydrangeas. Keep the visit low-impact and stay on marked paths.
cards.short_summary: A named Arboretum garden and gathering place at the northern path entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Noel Welcome Garden is the first garden on the Arboretum’s northern path and is described by the Arboretum as a gathering place for visitors.
cards.access_notes: The garden is within the Arboretum, which is open daily from sunrise to sunset.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented University Library study environments across campus, spanning quiet reading rooms, collaborative tables, and technology-focused spaces.

cards.title: ACES (Funk) Library Floors 2–4
cards.subtitle: ACES Library, 1101 S. Goodwin Ave., Urbana
cards.notes: Settle into the upper library floors when natural light matters. Bring a covered drink and use the six reservable rooms for planned group work.
cards.short_summary: A large, naturally lit library setting with both open seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists ACES (Funk) Library floors 2–4 as a 350-person study area with extensive natural light, covered drinks allowed, and six reservable rooms.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current library access and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Communications Library Room 39
cards.subtitle: Gregory Hall, Room 39
cards.notes: Use this Gregory Hall room for conversation-friendly work. Its listed activity level suits a project meeting or a study session with spoken discussion.
cards.short_summary: A communications-library room designed for active, collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Communications Library Room 39 in Gregory Hall as a 51-person, volume-level-3 study space with natural and overhead lighting; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current library access and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Communications Library Room 122
cards.subtitle: Gregory Hall, Room 122
cards.notes: Choose Room 122 for a smaller Gregory Hall session with daylight. Keep a covered drink handy and plan for a lower conversation level than Room 39.
cards.short_summary: A 40-seat, daylight-supported study room in the Communications Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Communications Library Room 122 in Gregory Hall as a 40-person, volume-level-2 study space with natural and overhead lighting; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current library access and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Grainger 1 West Design Space
cards.subtitle: Grainger Engineering Library Information Center, 1 West
cards.notes: Bring collaborators and working materials to this design-focused floor area. Food and drinks are permitted, and its listed activity level accommodates project noise.
cards.short_summary: A 120-seat Grainger setting intended for lively, design-oriented collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Grainger Engineering Library's 1 West Design Space as a 120-person, volume-level-4 area where food and drink are welcome.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Grainger Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: SSHEL Main Library Room 101
cards.subtitle: Social Sciences, Health, and Education Library, Main Library Room 101
cards.notes: Use the large-window seating in Room 101 for individual work with a conversational background. Keep beverages covered as required by the library listing.
cards.short_summary: A 67-seat SSHEL study area with ample window light.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists SSHEL Main Library Room 101 as a 67-person, volume-level-2 study space with substantial natural light; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: SSHEL Main Library Room 123
cards.subtitle: Social Sciences, Health, and Education Library, Main Library Room 123
cards.notes: Pick this compact SSHEL room when you need quiet shelves nearby. Talking is discouraged; bring only a covered drink and keep phone calls outside.
cards.short_summary: A 26-seat, low-volume SSHEL study area among the stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists SSHEL Main Library Room 123 as a 26-person, volume-level-1 study space with light from windows and overhead fixtures; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: The Orange Room
cards.subtitle: Teaching, Learning, and Academic Support, Main Library Rooms 100 and 112
cards.notes: Set up at the large tables for solo or team work, then reserve a study room if needed. Power outlets, printers, and short-term technology loans are nearby.
cards.short_summary: A bright first-floor hub with tables, power, reservable rooms, and library support nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library describes the Orange Room in Main Library rooms 100 and 112 as a large study space with large tables, ample power, reservable study rooms, printers, and short-term technology loans.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Main Library; study rooms are reservable. Check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Shebik Family Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Literature & Languages Library, Main Library
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing work to this low-volume room. Table lamps and indirect light offer an alternative to bright overhead-only study areas.
cards.short_summary: A 320-seat reading room combining natural light, table lamps, and a quiet-use expectation.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists the Shebik Family Reading Room in the Literature & Languages Library as a 320-person, volume-level-1 study space with natural light, table lamps, and low indirect lighting.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Central Access Services Room 204
cards.subtitle: Main Library Room 204
cards.notes: Use Room 204 for a study group that benefits from natural light and historic chandeliers. Food and drinks are allowed in this active-use Main Library space.
cards.short_summary: A 67-seat Main Library space pairing daylight with historic fixtures.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Central Access Services Main Library Room 204 as a 67-person, volume-level-3 study space with natural light and historic chandeliers; food and drink are welcome.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Media Commons Room 220
cards.subtitle: Main Library Room 220
cards.notes: Choose this media-oriented room for a group session requiring daylight and nearby reservable rooms. Use a covered drink and expect an active environment.
cards.short_summary: An 83-seat Media Commons study space with daylight and four reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Media Commons Main Library Room 220 as an 83-person, volume-level-4 study space with substantial natural light and four reservable rooms; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location and four reservable rooms; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along campus-edge corridors, each with one specific, source-backed reason to stop.

cards.title: Spurlock Museum
cards.subtitle: Gregory Street corridor, at Oregon Street
cards.notes: Enter from Gregory Street and use the galleries as a focused stop; the museum also has cultural gardens, a learning center, and an auditorium.
cards.short_summary: World-cultures galleries and museum spaces on the Gregory Street edge.
cards.evidence_claim: Spurlock Museum is at 600 S. Gregory St., at Gregory and Oregon streets, and offers permanent galleries, temporary exhibits, cultural gardens, a learning center, and an auditorium.
cards.access_notes: Check the museum visit page for current open days and visitor guidance.

cards.title: Krannert Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Peabody Drive corridor, at Sixth Street
cards.notes: Use the Peabody-and-Sixth corner for a self-paced gallery visit; ask the front desk for current exhibitions and visitor information.
cards.short_summary: A free public art museum on the Peabody Drive corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Krannert Art Museum is at the corner of Sixth Street and Peabody Drive, is always free and open to the public, and lists Tuesday–Saturday hours with Thursday evening hours during classes.
cards.source_title: Plan a Visit | Krannert Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday; Thursday hours extend to 8 p.m. when classes are in session. Confirm holiday closures before going.

cards.title: Activities and Recreation Center (ARC)
cards.subtitle: Peabody Drive corridor, near First Street
cards.notes: Check the ARC schedule before heading over, then choose a facility activity such as climbing, fitness, aquatics, or a court-based session.
cards.short_summary: Large recreation facility with climbing, wellness, and court spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The ARC at 201 E. Peabody Drive includes a climbing wall, bouldering cave, instructional kitchen, reflection room, locker rooms, and multipurpose rooms.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and program participation may depend on membership or event arrangements; consult Campus Recreation before visiting.

cards.title: Campus Recreation Center East (CRCE)
cards.subtitle: Gregory Drive corridor, near Goodwin Avenue
cards.notes: Use CRCE as the recreation stop on east Gregory; consult Campus Recreation for the current facility schedule and eligible activities.
cards.short_summary: Campus Recreation destination on the east Gregory Drive corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Illinois Campus Recreation facilities map lists Campus Recreation Center East at 1102 W. Gregory Drive in Urbana.
cards.access_notes: Check Campus Recreation for current operating hours, access rules, and program availability.

cards.title: Campus Bike Center
cards.subtitle: Gregory Drive corridor, east of First Street
cards.notes: Bring a bike question or repair goal and check the current schedule; the center is built around hands-on bicycle learning.
cards.short_summary: Hands-on bicycle learning on Gregory Drive.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation describes the Campus Bike Center as a University–Bike Project of Urbana collaboration offering hands-on experiential learning to help people fix bicycles.
cards.access_notes: The current Campus Recreation hours page lists the Campus Bike Center at 51 E. Gregory Drive; verify hours before arrival.

cards.title: Illini Grove
cards.subtitle: Pennsylvania Avenue corridor, near Lincoln Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a daytime outdoor stop around the courts and picnic area; reserve the pavilion in advance if you are organizing a group gathering.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor courts and picnic facilities along Pennsylvania Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation states that Illini Grove has a rentable pavilion with a grill and tables, plus basketball, sand volleyball, and tennis courts.
cards.access_notes: Pavilion use is by rental; court and site availability can vary with scheduled programs.

cards.title: University of Illinois Ice Arena
cards.subtitle: Armory Avenue corridor, east of First Street
cards.notes: Check the event calendar for a public-skate slot, then arrive ready to rent skates if needed; schedules change around rink events.
cards.short_summary: Public skating and Learn to Skate opportunities on Armory Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ice Arena at 406 E. Armory Ave. offers public skating and Learn to Skate programming; public skate, lunch skate, and extended lunch skate are open to students, staff, and the public.
cards.access_notes: Consult the Ice Arena calendar for specific public-skating dates and times. The source lists skate rental at $3.

cards.title: Japan House
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Avenue corridor, south of Kirby/Florida
cards.notes: Walk the gardens during daylight and review garden etiquette first; book ahead if you want a guided garden tour, class, or tea ceremony.
cards.short_summary: Japanese gardens and cultural programs on south Lincoln Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Japan House is at 2000 S. Lincoln Ave.; its gardens are open dawn to dusk for self-guided walks, while tours and tea ceremonies are available by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Gardens are open dawn to dusk; the tea garden’s rocky path closes during winter. Guided tours and tea ceremonies require appointments.

cards.title: Gies Memorial Stadium
cards.subtitle: First Street corridor, south of Kirby Avenue
cards.notes: Use First Street to locate the stadium exterior and consult the official athletics schedule or gameday information before attending an event.
cards.short_summary: Illinois football’s home field on South First Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Gies Memorial Stadium, home to Illinois football, is at 1402 S. First St. in Champaign and contains Zuppke Field.
cards.source_title: Gies Memorial Stadium - Facilities | University of Illinois Athletics
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is straightforward; event entry, tickets, and security procedures depend on the specific event.

cards.title: State Farm Center
cards.subtitle: First Street corridor, near Kirby Avenue
cards.notes: Check the venue calendar before making the walk; use the official event listing for entry timing, ticketing, bag rules, and accessibility details.
cards.short_summary: Event arena on the South First Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: State Farm Center is located at 1800 South First Street, Champaign, Illinois 61820.
cards.source_title: Connect With Us | State Farm Center
cards.access_notes: Venue access is event-specific; check the official State Farm Center calendar and event guidance before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Illinois traditions and recurring campus rituals, from Homecoming events to landmark lore and stadium performances.

cards.title: Illinois Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Weeklong alumni-and-campus celebration
cards.notes: Check the official schedule before heading out; the 2026 celebration runs September 27–October 3 and includes events across campus.
cards.short_summary: Illinois has held a multi-day Homecoming celebration since 1910.
cards.evidence_claim: University Archives identifies the 1910 Illinois event as an early multi-day Homecoming, while the official site lists the current annual weeklong celebration.
cards.access_notes: See the official schedule for event-specific locations, registration, and ticket requirements.

cards.title: Watch the fountain turn orange
cards.subtitle: Illinois Homecoming kickoff at Alice Campbell Alumni Center
cards.notes: Stop by the Alice Campbell Alumni Center during Homecoming kickoff to see the annual fountain dyeing and confirm timing on the event schedule.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming opens with the Alumni Center fountain dyed as part of the kickoff.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Homecoming page names the annual Alumni Center fountain dyeing as its Sunday kickoff event.
cards.access_notes: The official page says everyone is welcome to stop by; confirm the date and time for each year.

cards.title: Walk, roll, or run the Homecoming route
cards.subtitle: Anniversary Plaza to Alice Campbell Alumni Center
cards.notes: Use the posted Homecoming Run route from Anniversary Plaza to the Alumni Center; it is presented as a rain-or-shine walk, roll, jog, or run.
cards.short_summary: The annual Homecoming Run connects Anniversary Plaza and the Alumni Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Homecoming page invites participants to run, jog, walk, or roll from Anniversary Plaza to Alice Campbell Alumni Center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm event timing and any registration details on the official Homecoming site.

cards.title: Find a spot along the parade route
cards.subtitle: Kirby Avenue, Gregory Drive, and First Street
cards.notes: Check the annual route before you go; the 2026 parade starts at Kirby and Fourth, travels west on Gregory, then turns south on First.
cards.short_summary: A campus parade remains a recurring part of Illinois Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Homecoming page lists an annual Homecoming Parade and specifies its route through campus.
cards.access_notes: Use the official Homecoming schedule for start time, route changes, and viewing guidance.

cards.title: See the orange-and-blue card section
cards.subtitle: Memorial Stadium student cheering tradition
cards.notes: At a home football game, watch the designated student section assemble card displays; the University Library traces the tradition back to 1910.
cards.short_summary: Block I grew from a 1910 pep club into a long-running Illinois cheering tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: University Library archives state that Block I began as a 1910 student pep club and that orange-and-blue cards were introduced in 1926.
cards.source_title: More than Just a Cheering Section: The Block I
cards.access_notes: Requires access to a home football game; follow stadium instructions for the card display.

cards.title: Follow the wooden turtle rivalry trophy
cards.subtitle: Illinois–Ohio State football tradition
cards.notes: Look for coverage around the Illinois–Ohio State game; the wooden turtle is exchanged as the rivalry trophy rather than a live animal.
cards.short_summary: Illibuck is the Illinois–Ohio State rivalry trophy, now represented by wood.
cards.evidence_claim: University Archives documents that Illibuck began as a live turtle and became a wooden replica after the turtle died in 1927.
cards.access_notes: The exchange is tied to the Illinois–Ohio State football rivalry; game attendance requirements vary.

cards.title: Join the Three in One singalong
cards.subtitle: Marching Illini halftime performance
cards.notes: At halftime, listen for “The Pride of the Illini,” “March of the Illini,” and “Hail to the Orange”; participants traditionally stand and sing.
cards.short_summary: The Three in One is a traditional Marching Illini halftime medley.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library’s music collection describes Three in One as the traditional Marching Illini halftime performance and identifies its three songs.
cards.access_notes: Typically experienced during a home football game; consult game-day programming for the performance.

cards.title: Take the graduation Alma Mater photo
cards.subtitle: Alma Mater statue near Green and Wright
cards.notes: Around graduation, plan ahead for a photo with the robed Alma Mater statue; campus staff note that lines can wrap around the block.
cards.short_summary: Graduates traditionally line up for a photo with Alma Mater in graduation attire.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois GradLIFE states that students traditionally have their photograph taken with Alma Mater while the statue wears orange-and-blue graduation robes.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor landmark; graduation-period queues can be lengthy.

cards.title: Read the Eternal Flame’s disputed romance lore
cards.subtitle: Class of 1912 gift on the Main Quad
cards.notes: Visit the monument between Lincoln Hall and the English Building, but treat its eternal-love kiss story as campus lore rather than established fact.
cards.short_summary: The Eternal Flame’s romantic promise is a well-known but disputed Illinois legend.
cards.evidence_claim: The Daily Illini describes the Eternal Flame’s kiss-for-eternal-love story as a well-known but disputed myth and identifies it as the Class of 1912 gift.
cards.source_title: Burning question: Is Eternal Flame kiss of fate?
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus monument; no participation is required to appreciate the landmark and its lore.

cards.title: Spot the graduating-class gifts
cards.subtitle: Landmarks including Alma Mater, Altgeld Chimes, and Eternal Flame
cards.notes: Use campus walks to connect landmark plaques and histories: Illinois graduating classes gave works including Alma Mater, Altgeld chimes, and the Eternal Flame.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes historically left physical gifts that became campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Daily Illini reports that Illinois class gifts include Alma Mater, the Altgeld chimes, the Eternal Flame, Illini Grove barbecue pits, and Illini Union furniture.
cards.source_title: Class gifts connect old alumni to new Illini
cards.access_notes: These are separate public campus landmarks; observe any building access rules at individual sites.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A flexible, under-21-safe campus sequence built around documented landmarks, public collections, gardens, and recreation.

cards.title: Start at Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Green and Wright streets, Urbana
cards.notes: Begin with a look at Lorado Taft’s three-figure Alma Mater statue, then use the nearby campus streets to orient yourself before crossing into the Quad.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus landmark at the Quad entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois identifies the Alma Mater as an iconic university symbol; it was created by alumnus and sculptor Lorado Taft and depicts three women in scholastic robes.
cards.source_title: Community | Global Education and Training | Illinois
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; view from surrounding public walkways.

cards.title: Get oriented inside the Illini Union
cards.subtitle: 1401 W. Green Street, Urbana
cards.notes: Use the building maps to locate the main-level study areas and art gallery, then note the lower-level Rec Room and seating for a later stop.
cards.short_summary: A mapped campus hub with study, gallery, dining, and recreation areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Illini Union’s building information lists study spaces and an art gallery on the main level, plus the Rec Room, restaurants, and open seating on the lower level.
cards.access_notes: Check the Union’s current building and vendor hours before going.

cards.title: Walk the Main Quad
cards.subtitle: Between Illini Union and Foellinger Auditorium
cards.notes: Take the central lawn route from the Union toward Foellinger Auditorium, pausing to identify the buildings framing the campus’s principal quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: The central open space connecting two major campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois describes the Main Quad as an open grassy area at the heart of campus, anchored by the Illini Union to the north and Foellinger Auditorium to the south.
cards.source_title: Community | Global Education and Training | Illinois
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow posted campus rules and event setup boundaries.

cards.title: See Foellinger’s copper dome
cards.subtitle: 709 S. Mathews Avenue, Urbana
cards.notes: Continue to the south end of the Quad for an exterior look at Foellinger Auditorium, then check its schedule if you want to return for a public program.
cards.short_summary: A historic Quad auditorium used for classes and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Foellinger Auditorium has served as both classroom and performance space since its original 1907 dedication and is located at the south end of the Quad.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the suggested stop; entry depends on building access and scheduled events.

cards.title: View the Morrow Plots from the walkways
cards.subtitle: South Quad near the Undergraduate Library
cards.notes: Observe the plots from the surrounding paths and keep outside the research area; the site is visible year-round but is not open for entry.
cards.short_summary: A protected, active agricultural research landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois states that the Morrow Plots are visible to visitors year-round, but as an active research site and National Historic Landmark they are not open for entry.
cards.source_title: Contact | Morrow Plots | College of Agricultural, Consumer & Environmental Sciences | Illinois
cards.access_notes: View only from surrounding walkways; do not enter the plots.

cards.title: Settle into Main Library Room 220
cards.subtitle: 1408 W. Gregory Drive, Urbana
cards.notes: Use Room 220 for a short reset, choosing a table or reserving a study room if available; covered drinks are permitted in this specific space.
cards.short_summary: A documented Main Library study area with seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Library Room 220 has 83 seats, 29 tables, four reservable study rooms, and permits drinks in covered containers.
cards.source_title: Main Library – Room 220 | University Library | Illinois
cards.access_notes: Consult the page’s live hours before visiting; room availability can vary.

cards.title: Browse Krannert Art Museum galleries
cards.subtitle: 500 E. Peabody Drive, Champaign
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit during posted public hours, keep food and drinks out of the galleries, and take personal-use photos only where signage allows.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art museum with public galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Krannert Art Museum states that admission is always free and lists public hours Tuesday through Saturday, including Thursday evening hours when classes are in session.
cards.source_title: Know Before You Go | Krannert Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Check current hours before visiting; personal-use photography is permitted unless otherwise posted.

cards.title: Explore Spurlock Museum exhibits
cards.subtitle: 600 S. Gregory Street, Urbana
cards.notes: Add a museum stop for permanent or temporary exhibits, following the museum’s visitor guidance on photography, bags, food, and gallery conduct.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum presenting cultural collections and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spurlock Museum visitor brochure lists free general admission and describes permanent and temporary exhibits representing historic and contemporary peoples worldwide.
cards.access_notes: Review current museum hours before visiting; follow gallery rules for bags, food, and photography.

cards.title: Stroll the Japan House Gardens
cards.subtitle: 2000 S. Lincoln Avenue, Urbana
cards.notes: Make a daylight garden walk near the Arboretum, using the established paths and garden etiquette; the tea garden’s rocky path closes in winter.
cards.short_summary: A traditional Japanese garden open for self-guided strolling.
cards.evidence_claim: Japan House says visitors are welcome to walk through its gardens on their own from dawn to dusk, with the tea garden closed during winter for safety.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk; review garden etiquette and note that the tea garden’s rocky path closes in winter.

cards.title: End with a Rec Room game
cards.subtitle: Illini Union lower level, 1401 W. Green Street, Urbana
cards.notes: Meet up for bowling, pool, or air hockey in the Union Rec Room; confirm the day’s operating hours and rates before committing to an activity.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation space with bowling lanes, billiards, and games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Illini Union Rec Room offers 14 bowling lanes, billiards, air hockey, and other recreation; the bowling page lists per-game and shoe-rental rates.
cards.access_notes: Check current Rec Room hours and rates; bowling and games require payment.
